title: He's 15 Years and 99 Days Old. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Just Broke Sachin Tendulkar's 36-Year Record.
excerpt: The Rajasthan Royals prodigy received his India cap at Old Trafford on Saturday, becoming the youngest male cricketer to represent the country — and ending a debate that began the moment he hit 72 sixes in IPL 2026.
body:
Some records are meant to stand. Sachin Tendulkar's status as India's youngest international cricketer — 16 years and 205 days when he walked out against Pakistan in Karachi in November 1989 — was supposed to be one of them. For 36 years, through a revolution in white-ball cricket, through the rise and explosion of the IPL, through the emergence of dozens of prodigies, nobody came close.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi just did more than come close. He demolished it.

At 15 years and 99 days, the left-handed opener from Madhya Pradesh was presented his India cap by teammate Tilak Varma before the second T20I against England at Emirates Old Trafford on Saturday. He is now India's 122nd men's T20 international cricketer — and the youngest male player to represent the country across all formats.

## A Rise Unlike Anything Indian Cricket Has Seen

The noise around Sooryavanshi is not hype. It is earned. His IPL 2026 campaign with Rajasthan Royals was not merely impressive — it was historic. He finished as the tournament's leading run-scorer with 776 runs in 16 innings at a strike rate of 237.30. He hit 72 sixes, smashing Chris Gayle's long-standing record for the most in a single IPL season. He was named both the Most Valuable Player and the Best Emerging Player.

He is fourteen months older than some of the bowlers he dismantled. He took on Jasprit Bumrah — widely regarded as the world's best T20 bowler — and hit him for two sixes in five balls. He launched Josh Hazlewood for 19 runs in a single over. He hit Bhuvneshwar Kumar for back-to-back sixes as though it were a net session.

Kumar Sangakkara, Rajasthan's director of cricket, recalled how Sooryavanshi first came to the franchise's attention. "We had a text in 2022 or 2023 from one of our analysts at a high-performance centre in Nagpur," Sangakkara told Sky Sports. "He said there's this young kid — he would have been about 12 or 13 at the time — and he's incredibly talented. We were all like, 'really, what is this? It must be some kind of joke.' But no, they were very adamant we had to bring this guy in and have a look."

The look was enough.

## The Debate That Raged Before the Cap

Sooryavanshi's call-up to the senior squad for the Ireland and England tours was expected. His debut was not immediate. He was passed over for both T20Is against Ireland — where India lost the series 2-0 — and for the rain-washed first T20I against England at Chester-le-Street.

The omissions sparked a public backlash. Sunil Gavaskar and Ravi Shastri expressed displeasure. AB de Villiers questioned the decision. On Friday night, Sooryavanshi posted an Instagram story — a photo with the caption "New Chapter" — that set cricket social media ablaze with speculation.

India's bowling coach Morne Morkel had said just a day earlier that "the team doesn't want to make too many changes." But captain Shreyas Iyer, it appears, decided enough was enough.

"He completely deserves to be in the squad," Iyer said after winning the toss. "He's someone who doesn't take pressure at all. Has an unflinching nature. He's very well aware of what's going to come in these coming matches."

## What This Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs following Indian cricket from Houston watch parties and living room screens across the US, UK, and Canada, Sooryavanshi's debut carries a particular charge. This is not just a new player. This is a generational shift — a teenager whose career has been forged entirely in the IPL era, whose records were set before he could legally drive in most countries, and whose ceiling appears absurdly high.

Sooryavanshi was already the youngest player selected for India's senior squad, at 15 years and 71 days — breaking both Shafali Verma's and Tendulkar's records. His actual debut age of 15 years and 99 days undercuts Tendulkar by more than a full year.

England captain Harry Brook acknowledged the challenge. "Done some homework on Vaibhav, we have some tactical decisions. Just a matter of executing now," Brook said.

Josh Tongue also made his T20I debut for England in the same match. But the attention, rightly, belongs to the teenager from Vidisha who just rewrote the oldest page in Indian cricket's record book.

The five-match series continues at Trent Bridge on Tuesday, with further games in Bristol and Southampton. Whatever happens from here, the record is already written: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15 years and 99 days, India cap number 122.

Sachin's record lasted 36 years. It took a 15-year-old to break it.
